cover.brief: Leonardo da Vinci, studies of the Virgin and Child with a cat, c. 1478–81: one sheet holds many trial poses before one is chosen, so creativity reads as paced work, not a flash of talent.
c: File:Leonardo da Vinci - 1860,0616.98, Two studies of the Virgin and Child with a cat and three studies of the Child with a cat.jpg
File:Leonardo da Vinci, Study for the Madonna of the Cat (verso).jpg

analysis-model.brief: El Lissitzky, Beat the Whites with the Red Wedge, 1919–20: a poster whose language (geometric signs), medium (political poster) and support (printed sheet) can be named at a glance.
c: File:Beat the Whites with the Red Wedge.jpg

masterclass-1.brief: Michelangelo, studies for the Libyan Sibyl, c. 1510–11: the same figure, hand and foot tried again and again on one sheet until one solution is fixed — opening and closing inside one creative act.
c: File:Studies for the Libyan Sibyl (recto); Studies for the Libyan Sibyl and a small Sketch for a Seated Figure (verso) MET DP807402.jpg
File:Album of Forty-five Figure Studies MET DP102546.jpg

masterclass-2.brief: Katsushika Hokusai, a page of the Hokusai Manga sketchbooks (from 1814): many quick, varied figures on one page — fluency (many ideas), flexibility (many kinds) and elaboration made visible.
c: File:Schetsen van Hokusai - deel 2 Hokusai manga Katsushika iitsu iboku Hokusai manga nihen (titel op object), RP-P-2004-510.jpg

masterclass-3.brief: The Gem paper clip (1890s): the everyday object of the 'unusual uses' test, a reminder that a high score on such a toy task says little about talent in another field.

masterclass-4.brief: Auguste Rodin, The Thinker (modelled 1880–81): a figure halted in thought before any tool is picked up, to picture framing the unclear problem before choosing a technique.
c: File:Auguste Rodin - The Thinker - 1917.42 - Cleveland Museum of Art.tif

masterclass-5.brief: A pocket set of drawing instruments by Peter Dollond, London, c. 1755: tools that extend the hand but do not decide the line — a technique serves judgement, it does not replace it.
c: File:Pocket set of drawing instruments MET DP232308.jpg

masterclass-6.brief: A wall of sticky notes from an innovation workshop (2010s): the signature image of 'design thinking', shown so students can ask what craft the method's look may hide.
c: File:Post-It Notes Wall at the Fast Company Innovation Festival (30772875917).jpg

lab-1.brief: Marcel Duchamp, Fountain, 1917, in Alfred Stieglitz's photograph: a factory urinal signed 'R. Mutt' that changes meaning when it moves into an art exhibition — the readymade students research.
c: File:Marcel Duchamp, 1917, Fountain, photograph by Alfred Stieglitz.jpg

lab-2.brief: Theo van Doesburg and Kurt Schwitters, Kleine Dada Soirée poster, 1922: Dada typography that scrambles the rules of the poster, a Dada tactic students can link to a studio technique.
c: File:Theo van Doesburg and Kurt Schwitters, Kleine Dada Soirée (Small Dada Evening), 1922, NGA 154076.jpg
File:Grand opening of the first Dada exhibition, Berlin, 5 June 1920.jpg

cover.brief: Charles Darwin's 'I think' sketch in Notebook B, 1837: a branching tree that opens many lines and lets most of them end — generation and selection in one drawing.

analysis-model.brief: Georges Seurat, oil study for A Sunday on La Grande Jatte, 1884: one of dozens of studies made before the final painting, so we ask how many options were closed to reach it.
c: File:Study for "A Sunday on La Grande Jatte" MET DP259921.jpg
File:Georges Seurat - Étude pour "La Grande Jatte" (Study for "La Grande Jatte") - 1948-7 - Albright–Knox Art Gallery.tiff

masterclass-1.brief: Concept-art sheet for the Blender Studio short Sprite Fright (2021): many variants of one character's head drawn side by side before one is chosen — generate first, then select.

masterclass-2.brief: Leonardo da Vinci, a Codex Atlanticus sheet of machine studies, c. 1490s: ideas that differ in kind, not thirty versions of one — fluency only counts when it comes with flexibility.

masterclass-3.brief: A brainstorming wall of sticky notes (2014): early ideas kept on the wall without judging, so that less obvious ones have room to appear.

masterclass-4.brief: Brian Eno and Peter Schmidt's Oblique Strategies card deck (first published 1975): a prompt card that stages one cognitive move, like a thinking hat.
c: File:Oblique Strategies deck, PO Box, The Barbican, London, UK.jpg

masterclass-5.brief: A Pugh concept-selection matrix: options scored against named criteria, the convergent step made explicit before ranking.

masterclass-6.brief: Vincent van Gogh, Self-Portrait with Bandaged Ear, 1889: the icon of the 'tortured genius' myth that this slide questions — workshops train practice, they do not manufacture genius.
c: File:Vincent van Gogh - Self-portrait with bandaged ear (1889, Courtauld Institute).jpg
File:Vincent van Gogh - Self portrait with bandaged ear F529.jpg

lab-1.brief: Kōdō Sawaki seated in zazen, c. 1920: still, upright meditation with attention on breath and body, the posture of the guided concentration that opens the Lab.

lab-2.brief: A sample of mediumistic automatic writing reproduced in 1930: script produced without stopping to correct, the practice the Surrealists borrowed as écriture automatique.

cover.brief: The Wright brothers' 1902 glider in flight at Kitty Hawk: an idea made visible in material, learned from, and changed from the year before.
c: File:Gliding flight, Wright Glider, Kitty Hawk, NC. 1902.10459 A.S..jpg
File:1902 Wright Brothers' Glider Tests - GPN-2002-000125.jpg

analysis-model.brief: Theo van Doesburg, studies for Composition (The Cow), c. 1917–18: successive versions reduce a cow to planes, each one showing what the next version was trying to learn.
c: File:Cow by Theo van Doesburg Museum of Modern Art 227.1948.6.jpg
File:Cow by Theo van Doesburg Museum of Modern Art 25.1969.jpg

masterclass-1.brief: Antoni Gaudí's hanging string-and-weight model for the Colonia Güell church, photographed c. 1908: a rough model built early to ask a structural question in material form.
c: File:Paper prototype of website user interface, 2015-04-16.jpg

masterclass-2.brief: Beethoven's sketchbook for the Seventh Symphony, 1812: themes tried in several versions before any is judged final — a protected space for variation before decision.
c: File:Sketches for the second movement of Symphony no. 7, op. 92, Beethoven, Petter Sketchbook, 1812, musical autograph - Morgan Library & Museum - New York City - DSC06691.jpg

File:Sketches for the first movement of the Fifth Piano Concerto, op. 73, ('Emperor'), Beethoven, from the Grasnick 3 Sketchbook, 1808-1809, musical autograph - Morgan Library & Museum - New York City - DSC06698.jpg

masterclass-3.brief: Replica of the Wright brothers' 1901 wind tunnel: wing shapes tested against one question before the next glider was built, and testing stopped when the data answered it.

masterclass-4.brief: Alexander Graham Bell's laboratory notebook, March 1876: a quick sketch of the telephone transmitter that thinks the device through on paper before it is built.

masterclass-5.brief: Paul Klee, a page of the Pedagogical Sketchbook (1925): one line or form opened into several possible developments, a bounded way to widen the solution space.

masterclass-6.brief: Orville Wright's diary entry for 17 December 1903: a written record of what was tried, what happened and what was learned — reflection at a checkpoint.
c: File:Thomas Edison in the Chemistry Laboratory writing in his notebook about rubber experiments. (d1857f0fb1de47f0b31dd6ca657964f5).jpg

lab-1.brief: An early-19th-century design sheet with three chairs with curved backs: one problem answered three ways side by side, the model for three rough entry points.
c: File:Design for Three Chairs with Curved Backs (verso- Sketch for a Sideboard) MET DP807145.jpg

lab-2.brief: The Wright brothers' 1900 glider flown unmanned as a kite: one version tested against one question (does it lift?) before judging it and revising once.
c: File:Wright Glider being flown as a kite. -1900 10457 A.S..jpg

cover.brief: A generic iterative-process diagram (plan, design, implement, test, evaluate, loop back): a process trail drawn as a cycle, the object this lecture teaches you to analyse.

analysis-model.brief: Frank and Lillian Gilbreth's standard symbols for process charts, 1921: a notation for recording every step of a process in order, before anyone judges it.

masterclass-1.brief: Gilbreth process chart of the 'present method' for ordering blank forms, 1921: the task and its sequence written down step by step before a better method is proposed.
c: File:Process Chart for Ordering Blank Forms - Present Method, 1921.jpg

masterclass-2.brief: A Jacquard loom with its chain of punched cards (19th-century mechanism, National Museum of Scotland): the pattern code (language), weaving (medium) and card and cloth (support) are three different things.
c: File:A Jacquard loom showing information punchcards, National Museum of Scotland.jpg

masterclass-3.brief: Edgar Degas, album of forty-five figure studies, c. 1882: many poses opened quickly, a few later kept — divergent and convergent work inside one process.
c: File:Album of Forty-five Figure Studies MET DP102546.jpg

masterclass-4.brief: An early-19th-century design for six chairs with scarlet upholstery: many variants opened, but all inside one commission's constraints — divergence is a hallmark, closing under constraint finishes the job.
c: File:Design for Six Chairs with Scarlet Upholstery (verso- Sketch for Sofa) MET DP807166.jpg

masterclass-5.brief: Loïe Fuller's Serpentine Dance, Folies-Bergère poster/photograph, 1890s: silk, light and movement are the material in which the idea is composed.
c: File:La danse serpentine, Loïe Fuller et ses transformations.jpg

masterclass-6.brief: Alfred Binet's 1911 results table for the Binet–Simon scale: children ranked by scores on short tasks, a reminder that a score is not the designer in context.
c: File:Tableau de résultats au test de Binet-Simon.jpg

lab-1.brief: Gilbreth's proposed process chart for first orders, 1921: a shared process laid out step by step on one card, the model for filling the 8-step card together.
c: File:Proposed Process Chart for First Orders, 1921.jpg

lab-2.brief: A page of Paul Klee's Bauhaus teaching notebook, 1922: a maker's own trail of exercises and notes, the kind of record you analyse in your own Lab sequence.
